<module id="multi_pipe_4bit">
    <description>4-bit unsigned number pipeline multiplier with two levels of registers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[3:0]">Input signal representing the multiplicand with a data width of 4 bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[3:0]">Input signal representing the multiplier with a data width of 4 bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[7:0]">Product output signal with a data width of 8 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="size">4</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="partial_product" width="8" depth="4">Stores partial products.</register>
        <register id="accumulator" width="8">Accumulates the final product.</register>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Extension of input signals
        reg [7:0] mul_a_extended;
        reg [7:0] mul_b_extended;
        
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                mul_a_extended <= 8'd0;
                mul_b_extended <= 8'd0;
            end else begin
                mul_a_extended <= {4'b0000, mul_a};
                mul_b_extended <= {4'b0000, mul_b};
            end
        end
        
        // Generate partial products and accumulate them
        integer i;
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                for (i = 0; i < size; i = i + 1) begin
                    partial_product[i] <= 8'd0;
                end
                accumulator <= 8'd0;
            end else begin
                for (i = 0; i < size; i = i + 1) begin
                    if (mul_b_extended[3 - i]) begin
                        partial_product[i] <= mul_a_extended << i;
                    end else begin
                        partial_product[i] <= 8'd0;
                    end
                end
                accumulator <= partial_product[0];
                for (i = 1; i < size; i = i + 1) begin
                    accumulator <= accumulator + partial_product[i];
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Output the final product
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                mul_out <= 8'd0;
            end else begin
                mul_out <= accumulator;
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>
